A football is punted into the air. The graph shows the football’s height above the ground, in meters, at time [MATH: x] seconds after it is kicked. What is the best interpretation of the marked point [MATH: (2,\ 19.2)?]

sections.normalized_html:
We begin by interpreting each coordinate of the point [MATH: (2,\ 19.2){:}]

  • [MATH: x = 2] represents the time in seconds after the football was kicked.

  • [MATH: y = 19.2] represents the football’s height above the ground in meters at that moment.

Therefore, the point [MATH: (2,\ 19.2)] indicates the following:

[MATH: 2] seconds after it was kicked, the football’s height above the ground is [MATH: 19.2] meters.

sections.normalized_html: A soccer ball is kicked into the air. The graph shows the ball’s height above the ground, [MATH: y], in meters, [MATH: t] seconds after it was kicked. What is the best interpretation of the [MATH: x]-intercept of the graph?
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/35fa19be11f35eaf167b48a21fad94c4]

A soccer ball is kicked into the air. The graph shows the ball’s height above the ground, [MATH: y], in meters, [MATH: t] seconds after it was kicked. What is the best interpretation of the [MATH: x]-intercept of the graph?

sections.normalized_html:
The [MATH: x]-intercept of the graph is the point where the graph intersects the [MATH: x]-axis. This happens when the height is [MATH: 0,] which corresponds to the ball reaching the ground.

From the graph, we observe that the [MATH: x]-intercept occurs at approximately [MATH: t = 3,] which represents the amount of time that passed before the ball hit the ground.

Therefore, the best interpretation of the [MATH: x]-intercept of the graph is the following:

The ball hits the ground at [MATH: 3] seconds.

items.title: Interpreting the Y-Intercept of a Graph

sections.normalized_html: The graph shown gives the estimated number of bacteria in a refrigerated lab culture as a function of the number of hours since the culture was removed from the fridge. What is the best interpretation of the [MATH: y]-intercept of the graph in this context?
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/cb63d058f4b755a465bf2b57e0d212f7]

The graph shown gives the estimated number of bacteria in a refrigerated lab culture as a function of the number of hours since the culture was removed from the fridge.
What is the best interpretation of the [MATH: y]-intercept of the graph in this context?

sections.normalized_html:
The [MATH: y]-intercept of a graph of [MATH: y=f(x)] represents the value of [MATH: y] when [MATH: x=0.]

In this context, the variable [MATH: x] represents the number of hours since the culture was removed from the fridge, and [MATH: y] is the number of bacteria present in the culture.

So the [MATH: y]-intercept represents the number of bacteria at the moment the culture was removed from the fridge, i.e., when [MATH: x = 0.]

Looking at the graph, we can see that the point [MATH: (0, 340)] lies on the curve. This means there were [MATH: 340] bacteria at the start.

Therefore, the correct interpretation is as follows:

The estimated number of bacteria in the culture was [MATH: 340] when it was removed from the fridge.
